title: Magellan: A High-Performance Loop-Guided Prefetcher for Indirect Memory Access
problem: Graph analytics and sparse linear algebra applications rely heavily on indirect memory access (IMA), where pointer-chasing through irregular data structures causes frequent high-latency DRAM accesses due to poor temporal and spatial locality. Existing hardware and software prefetchers for IMA target narrow access patterns and struggle with complex nested-loop IMA patterns in sparse workloads.
method: Magellan is a compiler-based software prefetcher that constructs dependence graphs across loop levels to detect complex multi-level IMA patterns. It captures inner-outer loop semantics to schedule prefetches for both current and future loop iterations, inserting prefetch instructions ahead of the load chain. The compiler analysis extracts the indirection chains (e.g., A[B[i]]) across nested loop boundaries and emits prefetch instructions with appropriate software distances derived from loop trip counts and memory latency estimates.

title: HOOP: A Scalable Hybrid DC-DC Converter Ring for High-Performance Computing
problem: Multi-phase DC-DC converters for AI-era HPC require automatic current balancing across tens or hundreds of phases without complex digital control; hybrid topologies in parallel remain difficult to balance between converters.
method: HOOP: Hybrid converter with power ring (Φ0) for auto current balance and back ring (Φ0) for phase shedding. Leverages charge-balance properties of capacitors (similar to prior buck/three-level approaches) but extends to parallel hybrid converters via ring topology for inter-converter balancing.

title: Quorum: Zero-Training Unsupervised Anomaly Detection using Quantum Autoencoders
problem: Unsupervised anomaly detection requires training-free methods due to lack of labeled anomalies. Quantum machine learning models are hard to train (gradient computation), but unsupervised autoencoders might bypass this.
method: Quantum autoencoder framework (Quorum) designed for unsupervised anomaly detection without classical training. Abstract suggests leveraging quantum properties for dimensionality reduction and anomaly scoring without gradient-based optimization.

title: Precise exceptions in relaxed architectures
problem: The classical definition of precise exceptions assumes a sequential programmer's model and is inadequate for modern architectures like Arm-A that expose relaxed memory behavior; no formal specification exists for what exception precision means in a relaxed-memory setting.
method: The authors develop an axiomatic model for Arm-A precise exceptions in the relaxed-memory setting. They identify key phenomena—including relaxed behavior across exception boundaries, external aborts, and software-generated interrupts—that any definition must account for. A toolchain for axiomatic model execution is built, accompanied by a library of litmus tests that concretely characterize allowed and forbidden behaviors. The model is expressed in the style of existing Arm-A axiomatic memory models, extending them to cover exception entry and exit.

title: Cooperative Warp Execution in Tensor Core for RISC-V GPGPU
problem: Tensor cores integrated into RISC-V GPGPU architectures (e.g., Vortex) are severely under-utilized in many configurations, and simply increasing compute capacity does not yield proportional performance gains due to memory bandwidth limitations and warp divergence.
method: The paper integrates a tensor core into the open-source Vortex RISC-V GPGPU with a suite of GEMM intrinsics. Analysis of utilization identifies that memory bandwidth and warp-level resource contention bottleneck performance. The proposed cooperative warp execution mechanism allows multiple warps to share a single tensor core invocation, reducing per-warp memory requirements for GEMM operands and enabling better pipelining of data movement and computation. Hardware warp cooperation support is added to the tensor core datapath to manage the cooperative scheduling.

title: Late Breaking Results: A Geometric Diffusion Model for Macro Placement Generation
problem: Macro placement in VLSI design directly impacts circuit performance but remains a challenging optimization problem. Traditional approaches struggle to preserve circuit connectivity while satisfying placement constraints.
method: MacroDiff applies diffusion-based generative modeling capturing wirelength relationships as intermediate representation instead of directly predicting coordinates. Wirelength representation preserves circuit connectivity, reduces placement constraints, enhances solution flexibility, and naturally handles rotational/translational invariances.

title: Mitigating Routability Problems in Complementary-FET-based VLSI Designs
problem: Complementary FET (CFET) technology at sub-5nm scales stacks P-FET and N-FET for extreme cell area reduction, but reduced standard cell height creates routability challenges: limited pin accessibility and severe routing congestion due to constrained back-end-of-line (BEOL) routing resources.
method: Framework employs various pin-extended cells on demand to address pin accessibility and routing congestion. Partial placement blockages further alleviate routing congestion through strategic blocking of placement areas.

title: Swift or Exact? Boosting Efficient Microarchitecture DSE via Multi-fidelity Partial Order Prediction
problem: Microarchitecture design space exploration (DSE) is bottlenecked by slow synthesis and high-fidelity simulation (SPICE); early-stage PPA estimates are pessimistic and inaccurate, preventing rapid design iteration to find Pareto-optimal configurations.
method: Multi-fidelity optimization algorithm that fuses low-fidelity (fast, pessimistic) and high-fidelity (slow, accurate) PPA data using non-linear Gaussian process modeling. Introduces logical regression and multi-objective partial order relations to assess low-fidelity data reliability, reducing expensive high-fidelity evaluations while maximizing accuracy.

title: EXIST: Enabling Extremely Efficient Intra-Service Tracing Observability in Datacenters
problem: Intra-service application-level tracing imposes 5-10% average runtime overhead on traced applications (up to 18% worst case), making it impractical for continuous deployment in shared, stressed datacenters where sub-percent-level overhead is required for practical observability.
method: EXIST redesigns the intra-service tracing pipeline to achieve per-mille-level overhead through a combination of: extremely lightweight instrumentation hooks that avoid expensive context-switching or synchronization, asynchronous off-path trace collection and encoding that decouples tracing cost from the critical path, and selective event compression that preserves causality chains while discarding redundant intermediate events. The specific mechanism targets eliminating redundant data copies and reducing synchronization in the trace record path.

title: MoPAC: Efficiently Mitigating Rowhammer with Probabilistic Activation Counting
problem: DDR5 JEDEC's Per-Row Activation Counters (PRAC) introduce extended DRAM timing parameters that cause 10% average performance overhead for all applications—even benign ones—because counter updates are performed on every activation regardless of actual attack likelihood.
method: MoPAC reduces counter-update frequency by performing PRAC updates probabilistically rather than on every row activation. To maintain security, the mitigation threshold is adjusted downward by the inverse of the sampling probability to ensure aggressors are still caught before exceeding the Rowhammer threshold. MoPAC-C (memory-controller side) uses two precharge command variants: a normal-latency precharge that skips counter updates and a higher-latency precharge that performs counter updates, with the controller probabilistically selecting which to issue. MoPAC-D (in-DRAM) probabilistically selects activations for counter updates within the DRAM chip and uses ALERT or REF timing to absorb the counter-update latency.

title: Monolithic 3D FPGA Design and Synthesis with Back-End-of-Line Configuration Memories
problem: Conventional FPGAs use bulky Si SRAM for configuration, occupying area and increasing reconfigurable circuit overhead; this limits routing efficiency and increases latency for densely integrated FPGA designs.
method: Monolithic 3D FPGA uses amorphous oxide semiconductor (AOS) transistors in back-end-of-line (BEOL) layers: n-type (W-doped In₂O₃) and p-type (SnO) transistors replace bulky Si SRAM with lower-leakage configuration memory; AOS pass gates map FPGA switch/connection blocks above CLBs to increase proximity and reduce routing latency.

title: ReSMiPS: A ReRAM-based Sparse Mixed-precision Solver with Fast Matrix Reordering Algorithm
problem: Sparse matrix equation solvers on digital platforms suffer from memory bandwidth bottlenecks in large-scale storage and computation; ReRAM-based CIM offers promise but struggles to achieve high precision and energy efficiency simultaneously.
method: ReSMiPS combines a novel Fast Sparse Matrix Reordering (FSMR) algorithm with an In-memory float64 (IF64) data format implemented in analog ReRAM arrays, coupled with a hybrid-domain solution framework that performs floating-point sparse matrix operations directly in the ReRAM array.

title: 30.1 A 28Gb/mm24XX-Layer 1Tb 3b/Cell WF-Bonding 3D-NAND Flash with 5.6Gb/s/Pin IOs
problem: 3D NAND Flash scaling to higher layer counts (hundreds of layers) for density improvement creates multiple challenges: removal of dummy holes increases unselected string capacitance and power consumption; higher wordline counts amplify pass-voltage disturbance degrading cell reliability; increased wordline capacitance degrades program and read timing; high-speed I/O demands severe signal-integrity constraints.
method: 3D-NAND stack with WF-bonding (wafer-level) and multi-layer wordline architecture addressing: (1) dummy-hole removal via optimized cell-array design with high-density memory cells; (2) pass-voltage disturbance mitigation through efficient wordline structuring; (3) high-speed I/O support at 5.6Gb/s/pin via signal-integrity-aware pin design managing eye-width and eye-height constraints. Integration achieves 28Gb/mm2 at 3bits/cell (TLC NAND).

title: Late Breaking Results: Utilization of Hybrid Threshold-Voltage Flip-flops for Power Recovery
problem: Leakage power reduction in advanced technology nodes is challenging; multi-VT optimization can reduce leakage in non-critical paths, but critical-path sequential cells resist multi-VT optimization due to timing constraints.
method: Introduces hybrid-VT flip-flop cells where master and slave latches use different threshold voltages, allowing independent control of setup time and clock-to-Q delay. This decoupled control enables multi-VT optimization on critical paths without violating timing constraints. Hybrid-VT flip-flops can be applied to designs already optimized with conventional multi-VT cells.

title: Bootes: Boosting the Efficiency of Sparse Accelerators Using Spectral Clustering
problem: Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (SpGEMM) accelerators using row-wise product dataflow suffer from poor off-chip memory traffic because row reordering — the primary technique to improve data reuse — is either suboptimal, slow to compute, or fails to detect when reordering is counterproductive for certain sparsity patterns.
method: Bootes applies spectral clustering to reorder rows of the input matrix A before feeding them into a row-wise SpGEMM accelerator. A similarity matrix capturing structural properties of A's row sparsity patterns guides the clustering; similar rows are placed adjacent so that their accesses into B have high overlap, maximizing data reuse. The spectral clustering algorithm itself is optimized to reduce preprocessing time to a geometric mean of 11.61x faster than existing reordering techniques. A decision tree model trained on real-world sparse matrices predicts whether reordering will be beneficial before executing it, enabling cost-aware preprocessing that avoids overhead when reordering would increase traffic.

title: 37.1 IBM Telum II Processor Design-Technology Co-Optimizations for Power, Performance, Area, and Reliability
problem: Designing a high-performance 5nm processor at scale requires simultaneous optimization of power, performance, area, and reliability while managing massive concurrent EDA and design complexity across libraries, IP blocks, and gate-level entities.
method: IBM Telum II implements full-stack design-technology co-optimizations on modified 5nm Samsung bulk CMOS. Key innovations include: (1) new IBM-created standard cell and IP libraries optimized jointly with process node, (2) concurrent hierarchical design where arrays, regfiles, analog blocks, PHY, and custom logic design simultaneously rather than sequentially, (3) integrated modeling and abstraction layers to manage design data volume and complexity.
